'''Gavyn Sykes'''<ref name="KOTOBUKIYA" /> is a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served in the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces]] as an [[N-1 starfighter]] [[pilot]]. He flew in [[Bravo Squadron]] during the [[Invasion of Naboo]]<ref name="TPM" /> as [[Bravo Six]]. At the time, he had been assigned the [[astromech droid]] [[R2-C4 (Naboo)|R2-C4]].<ref name="KOTOBUKIYA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Gavyn Sykes first appeared as a supporting artiste in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], the first installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]].<ref name="TPM" /> Originally known as "Bravo Six," he was portrayed by the uncredited [[Wikipedia:British people|British]] actor [[Christian Simpson]]. He was first identified as [[Gavyn Sykes/Legends|Gavyn Sykes]] in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[2000]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo]]''.<ref name="Interview">{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsinterviews1|url=2010/02/christian-j-simpson-interview-star-wars.html|name=Star Wars Interviews|text=An interview with Christian Simpson}}</ref> In the current [[canon]], Sykes was first identified on the product page of an [[ARTFX+]] series R2-C4 figure released by the Japanese toy company [[Kotobukiya|KOTOBUKIYA CO., LTD]]. in [[December]] [[2014]]. On that page, he is referred to as '''ギャヴィン・サイケス''' in Japanese katakana characters, and the English spelling is not specified.<ref name="KOTOBUKIYA" />

Sykes was Simpson's first role in his career, being chosen during a casting session in [[Wikipedia:London|London]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]].<ref name="Interview" /> Simpson had seen an article in a newspaper that stated that actors were being scouted for the film so he contacted his acting agent<ref name="Caught on the Cam">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/bts/profile/f20050218/index.html|text=Caught on the Cam: Christian Simpson}}</ref> Laura<ref name="Fandom to Phantom">{{SW|url=news/from-fandom-to-phantom-when-star-wars-dreams-become-reality|text=From Fandom to ''Phantom'': When ''Star Wars'' Dreams Become Reality|nolive=1}}</ref> to whom he delivered his [[Wikipedia:Curriculum vitae|curriculum vitae]], letting her secure him the audition and eventually his casting.<ref name="Caught on the Cam" />  Simpson filmed several cockpit scenes, but those were cut due to time constraints.<ref name="Blog: The Beginning">{{Blog|bravo|1/comments|Making Episode III: 24 Jan 2003 - 'The Beginning'}}</ref> Simpson, however, can still be spotted twice in the film, first running to his first starfighter and then standing at the celebration ceremony in the line of the surviving pilots.<ref name="TPM" /> Although Simpson was uncredited for his portrayal as "Bravo Six,", he did receive a credit as a [[Wikipedia:Stand-in|stand-in]], which he personally discussed with producer [[Rick McCallum]].<ref name="Caught on the Cam" /> Simpson felt grateful at being featured in ''The Phantom Menace'', having dreamed since he was a child about being in a ''Star Wars'' film,<ref name="Blog: Just Call Me">{{Blog|bravo|7/comments|Making Episode III: 23 Aug 2004 - 'Just call me Hayden'}}</ref> being left with intense memories of the hangar scene's filming, as mini-explosive pellets were fired at his direction and even exploded on his hat, with sparks flying across his face and, since Skywalker's destruction of the droid control ship is viewed by some fans as his first step into his fall to the [[dark side of the Force]], Simpson jokingly apologized for Sykes being partially responsible for [[Darth]] Vader's creation.<ref name="Interview" /> Some fans queried if Sykes was canonically involved in Skywalker's victory due to his role not being clearly evident in the finished film, so when asked by a fan in his blog, Simpson asked [[Holocron continuity database]] keeper [[Leland Chee]] who verified and replied affirmatively.<ref name="Blog: The Beginning" />

Because of Simpson's involvement in ''The Phantom Menace'', McCallum would later contact him once more<ref name="Fandom to Phantom" /> to work as the stand-in of [[Hayden Christensen]]'s [[Anakin Skywalker]] in the [[2005]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]<ref name="Blog: The Callback">{{Blog|bravo|4/comments|Making Episode III: 11 Aug 2004 - 'The Callback'}}</ref> on the [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|United Kingdom]] set of the film<ref name="Fandom to Phantom" /> and being given a [[Star Wars: Blogs|VIP blog]] at [[StarWars.com]], where he was allowed to share behind-the-scenes information from the film's sets.<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|listing=true|bravo}}</ref> Simpson would later be invited to the premiere showing of ''Revenge of the Sith'' in [[Wikipedia:Berlin|Berlin]], [[Wikipedia:Germany|Germany]].<ref name="Fandom to Phantom" /> Simpson would later return to the franchise after [[The Walt Disney Company]]'s acquisition of [[Lucasfilm]], voicing [[alien]]s, [[First Order stormtrooper|stormtroopers]] and [[Resistance]] pilot [[C'ai Threnalli]] as well as co-producing [[Nien Nunb]]'s dialogue with [[Matthew Wood]] in the [[2015]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']],<ref name="SW-From Blast That X-wing! to Traitor!: The Voices of Star Wars: The Force Awakens">{{SW|url=news/from-blast-that-x-wing-to-traitor-the-voices-of-star-wars-the-force-awakens|text=From "Blast That X-wing!" to "Traitor!": The Voices of ''Star Wars: The Force Awakens''}}</ref><ref>{{Twitter|JATactor|status/677964176338235392|[[James Arnold Taylor]]|quote=Familiar voices are in that new movie! @MattLanter @cattaber @matthewood @MeredthSalenger @SamWitwer @DavidWCollins|archivedate=20181030001026}}</ref><ref name="SW-The Road to Rotich: Finding Nien Nunb, Part 1">{{SW|url=news/the-road-to-rotich-finding-nien-nunb-part-1|text=The Road to Rotich: Finding Nien Nunb, Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref><ref>{{Facebook|username=christianjsimpson|url=christianjsimpson/posts/10153874518182764|name=Christian Simpson|nobackup=1}}</ref> reprising his role as Threnalli again in the [[2016]] video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'',<ref>{{Facebook|username=chrisimpsonline|url=chrisimpsonline/photos/a.124024102763.103495.16384802763/10155206873437764|name=Christian Simpson|quote=A year ago today I recorded my part as X-Wing pilot C'ai Threnalli for LEGO Star Wars: #TheForceAwakens (though I couldn't tell you about it or they'd ship me to Abednedo) 🤐👽🚀 #MTFBWY!|archiveurl=https://archive.is/2amiH}}</ref> voicing one of [[Saw Gerrera]]'s rebels and some [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[Galactic Empire|Imperials]] in the 2016 [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Star Wars'' Anthology]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'',<ref>{{Facebook|username=chrisimpsonline|url=chrisimpsonline/photos/a.124024102763.103495.16384802763/10154891474117764|name=Christian Simpson|quote=A long time ago aged 7, I dreamt of being in A New Hope. I'm giddy to say that I'm now 10 minutes before it!|archiveurl=https://archive.is/Cw1Tl}}</ref> and co-scripting and directing Nien Nunb's dialogue for [[Kipsang Rotich]] for the [[2019]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']].<ref>{{Facebook|username=chrisimpsonline|url=chrisimpsonline/photos/wow-rise-of-skywalker-is-everything-you-wanted-a-new-star-wars-movie-to-be-every/10157974639592764|name=Christian Simpson|quote=Wow Rise of Skywalker is everything you wanted|nobackup=1}}</ref>

In his blog, Simpson expressed an interest in reprising his role as Gavyn Sykes again in the [[Star Wars: Underworld|live-action ''Star Wars'' television series]] that was being planned by [[George Lucas]] back in [[2009]].<ref name="Blog" /> However, Lucas announced the project to be on hold due to budget constraints in [[2010]]<ref name="rebelscum">
{{Rebelscum|url=story/front/TESB_30th_Anniversary_Screening_131186.asp|text=TESB 30th Anniversary Screening|date=2010-05-10}}</ref> and [[Pablo Hidalgo]] confirmed its cancellation in [[2012]] by 2019.<ref>{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/1084883854249189377|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=1313 as a show evaporated the second Grady Ranch as a production facility was rejected by the county.|archivefile=File:PabloTweet1-14-2019.png}}</ref>
